description: We are building health monitoring software for astronauts on space missions to protect crew safety and operational readiness. You should join us to work on a high-impact space exploration project that leverages real-time data, AI, and intuitive interfaces. We are looking for teammates skilled in AI/machine learning, data visualization, web development, astrophysics, and human factors.
summary: Astronaut Health Monitor is a web app that lets crew members track their own health during long missions and helps mission control spot problems early. Crew members log daily measurements, such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, temperature, sleep, mood, exercise, vision, cabin CO₂ and radiation, or let simulated sensors fill them in. Each reading is rated normal, caution or urgent, with a plain-language message and guidance for anything outside the normal range. A 3D body model and a habitat cabin view show where a problem is. Superadmins create crews, mission control manages its own crew, and crew members see only their own data
details: Astronaut Health Monitor is a web app that lets crew members on long space missions track their own health and helps mission control spot problems early. Crew members log daily measurements, or let simulated sensors fill them in, and each reading is rated normal, caution or urgent with a plain-language message and a suggested next step. A 3D body model and a habitat view show where a problem is, and an attention guide lists steps for anything outside the normal range. The superadmin creates crews and can set personal ranges for each crew member, mission control manages its own crew, and crew members see only their own data. The app is built with React, TypeScript, FastAPI and PostgreSQL, and one script sets it up with demo data. It is a hackathon prototype, not a medical device: its health ranges are estimates that have not been checked against sources, so they must not guide real decisions.
